quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: The vendor can either lower the price ___ throw in free shipping, but not both.
quests.completedSentence: The vendor can either lower the price or throw in free shipping, but not both.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But not both' confirms this is a genuine either-or choice, and 'either' always needs its fixed partner 'or' to express that.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'but not both' confirms only one of these two options will actually happen.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: In the negotiation, we can either extend the deadline ___ increase the budget to keep the same timeline.
quests.completedSentence: In the negotiation, we can either extend the deadline or increase the budget to keep the same timeline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two competing options are on the table here, and 'either' locks in 'or' as the only word that completes that choice correctly.
quests.nativeTip: Two possible negotiating moves are being weighed, and one will be chosen over the other.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: Either the two companies merge fully ___ they walk away from the deal entirely.
quests.completedSentence: Either the two companies merge fully or they walk away from the deal entirely.
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence presents two opposing final outcomes, and 'either' requires 'or' to hold that all-or-nothing choice together.
quests.nativeTip: These are two sharply opposite outcomes, and only one of them will happen.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither the CEO ___ her assistants were aware of the policy change until this morning.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the CEO nor her assistants were aware of the policy change until this morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither' still requires 'nor' even in a longer sentence like this; notice the verb 'were' matches the closer subject, 'assistants', which is typical in neither/nor sentences.
quests.nativeTip: Both people and their team share the same gap in knowledge here.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither the printer ___ the two scanners are functioning properly today.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the printer nor the two scanners are functioning properly today.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither' pairs only with 'nor'; here the verb 'are' agrees with the nearer subject, 'scanners', which is a natural feature of this structure.
quests.nativeTip: None of this office equipment is working, and both parts of that failure are being linked.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither my colleague ___ I were told about the change in plans.
quests.completedSentence: Neither my colleague nor I were told about the change in plans.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither' locks in 'nor' regardless of who the two subjects are; the verb here agrees with the closer subject, 'I'.
quests.nativeTip: Two people are equally left out of the loop, and that shared gap is being expressed.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Addition
quests.contextSentence: The new software update improves both speed ___ battery efficiency.
quests.completedSentence: The new software update improves both speed and battery efficiency.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two genuine improvements are being combined here, and 'both' always calls for its fixed partner 'and'.
quests.nativeTip: Two separate improvements are being credited to the same update.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Addition
quests.contextSentence: Both the marketing report ___ the financial summary need to be finalized before the board meeting.
quests.completedSentence: Both the marketing report and the financial summary need to be finalized before the board meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both documents are required together, not as alternatives, which is why 'both' pairs with 'and' rather than a choice word.
quests.nativeTip: Two documents are being grouped together as equally necessary.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Addition
quests.contextSentence: The app now supports both fingerprint login ___ facial recognition.
quests.completedSentence: The app now supports both fingerprint login and facial recognition.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since both login methods are actually supported at once, 'both' requires 'and' rather than a word that would suggest picking just one.
quests.nativeTip: Both login methods are genuinely available together, not as a single either-or choice.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: The manager not only approved the budget increase but ___ fast-tracked the hiring process.
quests.completedSentence: The manager not only approved the budget increase but also fast-tracked the hiring process.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Not only' teams up with 'but also' as a fixed phrase, so once 'but' has appeared, 'also' is the word needed to complete it.
quests.nativeTip: The word right before the blank is 'but', which is already halfway through its usual partner phrase.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: The renovation not only fixed the leaking roof but ___ upgraded the insulation throughout the building.
quests.completedSentence: The renovation not only fixed the leaking roof but also upgraded the insulation throughout the building.
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'not only... but', the fixed phrase is completed with 'also', adding this second upgrade to the first.
quests.nativeTip: A second improvement is being stacked onto the first, completing the usual phrase after 'but'.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: The keynote speaker not only inspired the audience but ___ left them with a clear plan of action.
quests.completedSentence: The keynote speaker not only inspired the audience but also left them with a clear plan of action.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is the standard 'not only... but also' pattern, and 'also' is what completes it once 'but' has already appeared.
quests.nativeTip: A second, practical benefit is being added right after the word 'but'.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: We need to finalize the guest list ___ or not everyone has RSVP'd yet.
quests.completedSentence: We need to finalize the guest list whether or not everyone has RSVP'd yet.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Or not' is the fixed tail that only pairs with 'whether'; 'if' cannot correctly attach to 'or not' in this way.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'or not' right after the blank only ever completes one particular word.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: The policy applies ___ or not employees have official contracts.
quests.completedSentence: The policy applies whether or not employees have official contracts.
quests.ruleExplanation: Only 'whether' correctly pairs with the fixed phrase 'or not' here; the other options can't grammatically attach to it this way.
quests.nativeTip: The words 'or not' immediately after the blank point to one specific required partner.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: Please confirm whether you'll join us in person ___ dial in remotely.
quests.completedSentence: Please confirm whether you'll join us in person or dial in remotely.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here 'whether' introduces two named alternatives rather than the fixed 'or not' phrase, and that structure still needs to be completed with 'or'.
quests.nativeTip: Two specific ways of joining are being named as the two possibilities.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: You can either accept the offer as it stands ___ reject it outright — there's no room for negotiation.
quests.completedSentence: You can either accept the offer as it stands or reject it outright — there's no room for negotiation.
quests.ruleExplanation: It's tempting to reach for 'nor' because 'reject' sounds negative, but 'either' always requires 'or', no matter how negative the options themselves are.
quests.nativeTip: Even though the second option sounds negative, 'either' still only ever pairs with one particular word.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: The form asks you to either confirm your attendance ___ decline the invitation by Friday.
quests.completedSentence: The form asks you to either confirm your attendance or decline the invitation by Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Decline' being negative doesn't change the required pairing — 'either' always needs 'or', not 'nor'.
quests.nativeTip: One option is positive and one is negative, but that doesn't change which word 'either' needs.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: Either you cancel the subscription before the trial ends ___ you'll be charged automatically.
quests.completedSentence: Either you cancel the subscription before the trial ends or you'll be charged automatically.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even in this if-you-don't warning, 'either' still requires its fixed partner 'or', not 'nor'.
quests.nativeTip: This warns of an automatic consequence, but the word pairing with 'either' never changes.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither the hotel ___ the airline offered any compensation for the delay.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the hotel nor the airline offered any compensation for the delay.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither' only ever pairs with 'nor', even though 'or' might feel tempting since the sentence describes a plain lack of compensation.
quests.nativeTip: Both companies equally failed to do something here, and 'neither' always needs one specific partner.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither apologizing ___ offering a discount fixed the customer's frustration.
quests.completedSentence: Neither apologizing nor offering a discount fixed the customer's frustration.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both attempted solutions are being described as failures together, which requires 'nor' to match 'neither', not 'or'.
quests.nativeTip: Two attempted fixes both failed, and that shared failure needs its one matching word.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither the software update ___ the hardware fix solved the crashing issue.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the software update nor the hardware fix solved the crashing issue.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'neither' already opened the sentence, only 'nor' can correctly complete this shared-failure structure.
quests.nativeTip: Two attempted technical solutions both came up short, and that shared shortfall pairs with only one word.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: Not only did the merger boost quarterly revenue, ___ it also strengthened the company's market position.
quests.completedSentence: Not only did the merger boost quarterly revenue, but it also strengthened the company's market position.
quests.ruleExplanation: This formal opening with 'not only' and inverted word order calls for 'but' to introduce the second benefit that follows.
quests.nativeTip: A second, equally important benefit is following the formal, inverted opening.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: Not only does the new policy cut costs, ___ it also simplifies the approval process for everyone.
quests.completedSentence: Not only does the new policy cut costs, but it also simplifies the approval process for everyone.
quests.ruleExplanation: The inverted structure after 'not only' requires 'but' to introduce this second benefit.
quests.nativeTip: A second advantage is being added after this formal, inverted opening.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: Not only was the client impressed with the proposal, ___ she also recommended the firm to two colleagues.
quests.completedSentence: Not only was the client impressed with the proposal, but she also recommended the firm to two colleagues.
quests.ruleExplanation: The formal, inverted 'not only' opening pairs with 'but' to introduce this second, even more valuable outcome.
quests.nativeTip: A stronger, more valuable outcome is being added right after the formal opening.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: Customers can either exchange the item for store credit ___ request a full refund within thirty days.
quests.completedSentence: Customers can either exchange the item for store credit or request a full refund within thirty days.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two genuine customer options are being laid out, and 'either' requires its fixed partner 'or' to present that choice.
quests.nativeTip: Two customer options are being offered, and one will be chosen over the other.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: The support team couldn't confirm whether the refund had processed ___ was still pending review.
quests.completedSentence: The support team couldn't confirm whether the refund had processed or was still pending review.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is genuine uncertainty between two named statuses, and 'whether' requires 'or' to complete that pair.
quests.nativeTip: Two possible statuses are being weighed, and the team simply isn't sure which one is true.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Addition
quests.contextSentence: The new policy benefits both loyal customers ___ first-time buyers alike.
quests.completedSentence: The new policy benefits both loyal customers and first-time buyers alike.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both groups genuinely benefit together, not as alternatives, so 'both' pairs with 'and' here as always.
quests.nativeTip: Two different groups are both gaining from this policy at the same time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: Neither the budget ___ the timeline allows for any further delays.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the budget nor the timeline allows for any further delays.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both constraints are being described as equally strict, which requires 'nor' to match the negative opening word 'neither'.
quests.nativeTip: Two project constraints are both equally strict here, with no room to spare.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Emphatic Addition
quests.contextSentence: The candidate not only met every requirement but ___ exceeded expectations in the interview.
quests.completedSentence: The candidate not only met every requirement but also exceeded expectations in the interview.
quests.ruleExplanation: Once 'not only... but' has appeared, 'also' is the word that completes that fixed phrase and introduces the stronger fact.
quests.nativeTip: A stronger, more impressive fact follows right after the word 'but'.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: You can either renew your membership online ___ visit the front desk in person.
quests.completedSentence: You can either renew your membership online or visit the front desk in person.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two separate, equally valid renewal methods are being presented, and 'either' still requires 'or' to complete that choice.
quests.nativeTip: Two ways of renewing are being offered, and either one works on its own.
